references.text: The introduction to the chapter describing the laws about clean and unclean animals, as summarized in verse 46.
The laws concerning birds (העוף) mentioned in the summary of verse 46.
The laws regarding water-dwelling creatures (הרמשת במים) referred to in verse 46.
The laws about creeping things on the ground (השרצת על־הארץ) mentioned in the summary.
The verses just before the summary that deal with reptiles and the purpose of the purity laws.
A parallel list of clean and unclean animals in Deuteronomy that complements Leviticus 11.
The creation of animals, birds, and water-dwelling creatures—the same categories mentioned in verse 46.
Noah's ark and the distinction between clean and unclean animals, an early reference to the categories in Leviticus 11.
Ezekiel refers to purity laws and unclean animals in connection with the prophet's protest.
Peter's vision concerning clean and unclean animals, which refers back to the laws in Leviticus 11.
Peter recounts the vision involving four-footed animals, creeping things, and birds—the categories from Leviticus 11:46.
